NOTICE SERVED for the Opponent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE THE ACTING CHIEF JUSTICE MR.
 JAYANT PATEL  and  HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE VIPUL M. PANCHOLI

Date : 07/01/2016  ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE ACTING CHIEF JUSTICE MR. JAYANT PATEL)
1.

The petitioners have approached to this Court for espousing the public cause contending inter-alia that Jersey cow milk (hereinafter referred to as 'A1 milk') contains certain harmful element to the human in comparison to normal milk of Indian cow (hereinafter referred to as 'A2 milk').
The prayers are made to issue appropriate writ, to direct respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 to take effective steps to rule out the sale and circulation of A1 milk and its product.
The other prayers are also made by the petitioners based on the aforesaid principal prayer.

2. We have heard Mr. Pathak, learned counsel HC-NIC Page 1 of 4 Created On Sat Jan 09 01:50:09 IST 2016 C/WPPIL/91/2015 ORDER appearing for the petitioners, Mr. Parth Bhatt appearing for Chintan Praveenbhai Gohel & 2 vs State Of Gujarat & 4....Opponent(S) on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52620688/
1

sentences.text: respondent No.2 and Mr. Devnani appearing for the State Government.

3. When we have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it appears that as per Mr.
Pathak, A1 milk is harmful and it contains certain components rather known as beta-casein protein which is harmful to the human body in comparison to the contents of beta-casein protein in A2 milk.

The grievance on the part of the petitioner is that A1 milk and milk product should not be marketed and it is alternatively contended that even if they are to be marketed, the consumer should be made to know that A1 milk contains particular percentage of beta-casein and the milk is of Jersey cow as A1 milk so that the consumer may decide whether to go for A1 milk or A2 milk.
4. On behalf of the Union of India, affidavit-in- reply has been filed, wherein it has been contended that it is not scientifically proved that A1 milk is harmful to the human body.

It is further contended that the report which has been relied upon by the petitioners in the petition is on the basis of the test conducted upon the animal and not the human body and there is no conclusive evidence available to show that A1 milk is harmful to the human body.
On behalf of the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India, the appearance is filed by Mr. Saiyad but reply has not been filed.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standard Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 5. The aforesaid prima facie goes to show that there HC-NIC Page 2 of 4 Created On Sat Jan 09 01:50:09 IST 2016 C/WPPIL/91/2015 ORDER is no scientifically established evidence available in the record of the present proceedings to show that A1 milk is susceptible to the health risk of a human body based on the contents of beta-casein.

However, at the same time there is no sufficient material in the present proceedings for any scientific test undertaken upon the human body for the adverse effect of A1 milk or A2 milk, as the case may be.

If the petitioners find that they have authenticated scientific material to show the risk factor in the consumption of A1 milk by the human beings, it would be for the petitioners to approach before the Central Advisory Committee constituted under Section 11 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').
The function of the Central Advisory Committee inter-alia as per Section 12 of the Act is to identify the potential risk in any food.
It is undisputed position that the petitioners have not approached before such authority.

6. Further, the grievance on the part of the petitioners is that in the branding of the product there should be with specific disclosure of the milk as that of A1 or A2 and the contents of beta-casein.
Such grievance may fall in the arena of Section 23 of the Act.

Further, as per Section 29 of the Act,
the Statutory Authorities are constituted and formed with the powers for enforcement of the Act viz.
food authority at the Central level and food authority at the State level.

The petitioners, if find, that there is misbranding or incorrect branding or there should HC-NIC Page 3 of 4 Created On Sat Jan 09 01:50:09 IST 2016 C/WPPIL/91/2015 ORDER be proper branding when the milk is marketed, it would be for the petitioners to approach before the State Food Safety Authority as per Section 29 of the Act.
It is undisputed position that the petitioners have up till now not approached before such authority.
7. In view of the above, we are not inclined to entertain the petition at this stage.

However, it is observed that if the petitioners ventilate their grievance/s before the above referred authority, the concerned authority shall examine the matter in accordance with law and appropriate action may be Chintan Praveenbhai Gohel & 2 vs State Of Gujarat & 4....Opponent(S) on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52620688/
2 taken if at all ultimately required.

entities.text: Chintan Praveenbhai Gohel & 2 vs State Of Gujarat & 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also clarified that such authority, if find proper, may take help of the Scientific Committee which is even otherwise also to assist the Central Advisory Committee as per the provisions of the Act.
8. No further order deserves to be passed.
Hence, petition disposed of accordingly.
(JAYANT PATEL, ACJ.) (VIPUL M. PANCHOLI, J.)
